note: [agent-bulk] nuecc, 24 showers, 2 in scope. Verdict shower 18092 (pdg 11, kine_charge 604.0, 34 seg) -- the first pdg-11 entry of in_scope and also the highest-charge object. The other in-scope object 18009 (pdg 13, kine_charge 74.2, 64.8 cm) is discussed below; the 22 skipped showers are all sub-20 MeV and I did not look at them. Vertex judged off the vtx-* sweep at 137.9 cm half-span (r95 110.3, under the 150 cm trigger so no vtxz-* frames were written). OVER-CLUSTERED: 18092's member set contains a backward branch that its own cone does not reach. Taking the shower's own axis as vertex -> centroid of the other 32 members, direction (-0.043,-0.426,0.904), those 32 members lie at 0.3-47.3 deg from it (only the seed 18092 at the vertex reaches 47, everything else is under 16 deg) and run out to 137 cm -- a tight, coherent cone. Against that same axis 18015 sits at 129-179 deg and 18008 at 176-179 deg, i.e. directly BEHIND the shower start. They are also detached from the shower's own body: nearest member point 10.9 cm away for 18015 and 14.7 cm for 18008, while both touch the 64.8 cm pdg-13 track 18009 (gap 0.25 cm and 0.00 cm -- 18008's endpoint IS 18009's endpoint at (120.0,142.4,348.2)). Neither entered through the cone: the acceptance plot shows them at 13 cm/33.5 deg and 15 cm/58 deg, both above the 30 deg pass-1 box, absorbed by pass3_cluster_map (direct) and conn3_unreachable (walk_add). MARKS, and they differ in strength (correction 7): 18015 OUT is the strong one -- 17.3 cm, 30 fitted points, owned only by 18092, and the one that carries the charge. 18008 OUT is the weak one and the one I would let the owner reverse: it is 5.4 cm and it is ALSO one of 18009's two members (18009 nseg 2, owner-grouped 1, cmp_div 2), so it is a shared segment in correction-11's sense, not something 18092 took from a neighbour. NOT under-clustered: every unowned segment near the shower is a 0.1-1.2 cm two-point stub, the closest sitting 5.4 cm off the member set, and the nearest substantial ones are 8.5-9.4 cm out. Membership triple-checked for 18092: nseg 34 == owner-grouped 34 == cmp_div 34 (0.0-137.0 cm, 0.0-126.3 deg -- that 126 deg is measured against the RECO axis, which is wrong; see next). START/AXIS WRONG on 18092 as well: the reco axis points roughly opposite to the shower's own body, which is why almost every genuine member is tabulated at 106-126 deg and was let in by pass3_cone rather than by any pass-1 step. THE SECOND FINDING I COULD NOT SETTLE, and the reason this is 'likely' not 'certain': 18009 is a 64.8 cm pdg-13 skeleton running at only 10 deg to the shower body, passing within 1.8 cm of the vertex and lying INSIDE the same dense charge blob as 18092's own skeleton -- two parallel skeletons in one blob. Either it is a genuine second particle, or it is the electron's own MIP stem split off from its shower, in which case 18092 is also under-clustered and the verdict would be 'both'. I could not separate those two readings from the three viewpoints I looked at, so I recorded only the finding I could measure. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
